claim: C0 reflow keeps old classes stable while adding new ones; the random-add baseline risks the new anchor landing on an existing class
verdict: MIXED / NOT UNIFORMLY SUPPORTED: reflow does keep the layout separated (min_d 0.49-0.80 across growth vs 0.25-0.54 for random-add) but random-add does NOT risk collision at this noise and scale, and it achieves equal-or-better routing: new-class acc random-add wins or ties 4/5 stages (0.950/0.950/0.970 vs 0.780/0.780/0.960 reflow at k=6,7,10) and all-class acc random-add wins 3/5 (0.980/0.987/0.973 vs 0.973/0.967/0.953). Reflow's advantage shows only where random-add draws a weak position (k=8: 0.720, k=9: 0.600). The displacement cost of reflow (0.16-0.28) buys separation, not routing.
